phrases.arabic: قَبْلَ أَمْسِ كَانَ عِنْدِي عَمَلٌ حَتَّى الْمَسَاء

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: مَرْحَبًا يَا نُور. مَاذَا فَعَلْتِ أَمْسِ؟
dialogue.transliteration: marhaban yaa Noor. maadhaa fa3alti amsi?
dialogue.english: Hello, Noor. What did you do yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: أَهْلًا يَا خَالِد. كَانَ أَمْسِ يَوْمًا طَوِيلًا جِدًّا.
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan yaa Khaalid. kaana amsi yawman taweelan jiddan.
dialogue.english: Hello, Khalid. Yesterday was a very long day.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: لِمَاذَا؟
dialogue.english: Why?

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: اِسْتَيْقَظْتُ مُتَأَخِّرَةً، ثُمَّ ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الْعَمَل.
dialogue.transliteration: istayqadtu muta2akhkhiratan, thumma dhahabtu ilaa al-3amal.
dialogue.english: I woke up late, then I went to work.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: وَأَيْنَ كُنْتِ لَيْلَةَ أَمْسِ؟
dialogue.english: And where were you last night?

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: كُنْتُ فِي الْبَيْتِ. تَعِبْتُ كَثِيرًا مِنَ الْعَمَل.
dialogue.transliteration: kuntu fee al-bayti. ta3ibtu katheeran mina al-3amal.
dialogue.english: I was at home. I got very tired from work.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: هَلِ اشْتَرَيْتِ شَيْئًا أَمْسِ؟
dialogue.english: Did you buy anything yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، اشْتَرَيْتُ قَمِيصًا جَدِيدًا.
dialogue.english: Yes, I bought a new shirt.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: وَمَنْ رَأَيْتِ أَمْسِ؟
dialogue.english: And who did you see yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: رَأَيْتُ أُخْتِي، وَأَكَلْنَا فِي مَطْعَمٍ جَمِيل.
dialogue.transliteration: ra2aytu ukhtee, wa akalnaa fee mat3amin jameel.
dialogue.english: I saw my sister, and we ate at a nice restaurant.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: وَكَيْفَ كَانَ الْجَوُّ؟
dialogue.english: And how was the weather?

lessons.culture: In Fusha the past is told with the past-tense verb and أَمْسِ for yesterday, the same words a news reader uses for the day before. Friends ask about last night with a full question such as أَيْنَ كُنْتَ؟ and answer in one short past-tense sentence.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks you: 'مَاذَا فَعَلْتَ أَمْسِ؟'. Say you went to the market.
exercises.tip: ذَهَبْتُ is 'I went'; the ending تُ marks 'I' in the past.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks you: 'أَيْنَ كُنْتَ لَيْلَةَ أَمْسِ؟'. Say you were at home.
exercises.tip: كُنْتُ is 'I was'; in the question it is كُنْتَ for 'you were' (to a man).

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'مَاذَا _____ أَمْسِ؟' (What did you do yesterday? to a man)
exercises.tip: فَعَلْتَ is 'you did' to a man; to a woman it is فَعَلْتِ.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'كَانَ _____ يَوْمًا طَوِيلًا جِدًّا.' (Yesterday was a very long day.)
exercises.tip: أَمْسِ means 'yesterday'; قَبْلَ أَمْسِ means 'the day before yesterday'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Who did you see yesterday?' (to a man)
exercises.tip: مَنْ is 'who'; the past verb رَأَيْتَ comes straight after it.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'I woke up late yesterday.'
exercises.tip: مُتَأَخِّرًا means 'late'; a woman says مُتَأَخِّرَةً.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Did you buy anything yesterday?' (to a man)
exercises.tip: هَلْ opens a yes-or-no question; before اشْتَرَيْتَ it becomes هَلِ.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'Why didn't you come yesterday?'
exercises.tip: لِمَاذَا is 'why'; لَمْ makes the verb a past negative.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'yesterday'?
exercises.tip: غَدًا is tomorrow, الْيَوْم is today, أَمْسِ is yesterday.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'أَمْسِ / فَعَلْتَ / مَاذَا'.
exercises.tip: Question word first, then the verb, then the time.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'جِدًّا / كَانَ / أَمْسِ / الْجَوُّ / جَمِيلًا'.
exercises.tip: كَانَ comes first, then the thing described, then what it was like.

phrases.arabic: عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ صَغِيرًا، كُنْتُ أُحِبُّ اللَّعِبَ خَارِجَ الْبَيْت
phrases.transliteration: 3indamaa kuntu sagheeran, kuntu uhibbu al-la3iba khaarija al-bayt

phrases.arabic: نَشَأْتُ فِي حَيٍّ قَدِيمٍ فِي دِمَشْق
كُنَّا نَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ فِي الزُّقَاق
phrases.transliteration: kunnaa nal3abu kurata al-qadami fee az-zuqaaq

phrases.arabic: فِي كُلِّ صَيْفٍ كُنَّا نَذْهَبُ إِلَى بَيْتِ جَدِّي فِي الْقَرْيَة
phrases.transliteration: fee kulli sayfin kunnaa nadh-habu ilaa bayti jaddee fee al-qarya

phrases.arabic: كَانَتْ جَدَّتِي تَحْكِي لَنَا قِصَصًا قَبْلَ النَّوْم
phrases.transliteration: kaanat jaddatee ta7kee lanaa qisasan qabla an-nawm

phrases.arabic: كُنْتُ أَخَافُ مِنَ الظَّلَامِ كَثِيرًا وَأَنَا صَغِير
phrases.transliteration: kuntu akhaafu mina az-zalaami katheeran wa anaa sagheer

phrases.arabic: كَانَ مُعَلِّمِي فِي الْمَدْرَسَةِ لَطِيفًا جِدًّا
phrases.transliteration: kaana mu3allimee fee al-madrasati lateefan jiddan

phrases.arabic: كُنَّا نَمْشِي إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ مَعًا كُلَّ يَوْم
phrases.transliteration: kunnaa namshee ilaa al-madrasati ma3an kulla yawm

phrases.arabic: عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ صَغِيرًا، كُنْتُ أَحْلُمُ بِأَنْ أُصْبِحَ طَيَّارًا
phrases.transliteration: 3indamaa kuntu sagheeran, kuntu a7lumu bi2an usbi7a tayyaaran

phrases.arabic: فِي ذَلِكَ الْوَقْتِ كَانَتِ الْحَيَاةُ أَبْسَطَ بِكَثِير
phrases.transliteration: fee dhaalika al-waqti kaanati al-7ayaatu absata bikatheer

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: حَدِّثِينِي عَنْ طُفُولَتِكِ يَا هَالَة. أَيْنَ نَشَأْتِ؟
dialogue.english: Tell me about your childhood, Hala. Where did you grow up?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وَمَاذَا كُنْتِ تَفْعَلِينَ هُنَاكَ؟
dialogue.english: And what did you used to do there?

dialogue.speaker: Hala
dialogue.arabic: كُنْتُ أَلْعَبُ مَعَ صَدِيقِي كَرِيم فِي الزُّقَاق.
dialogue.transliteration: kuntu al3abu ma3a sadeeqee Kareem fee az-zuqaaq.
dialogue.english: I used to play with my friend Kareem in the alley.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: هَلْ كُنْتُمْ تَلْعَبُونَ كُرَةَ الْقَدَم؟
dialogue.english: Did you used to play soccer?

dialogue.speaker: Hala
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، كُنَّا نَلْعَبُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ بَعْدَ الْمَدْرَسَة.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, kunnaa nal3abu kulla yawmin ba3da al-madrasa.
dialogue.english: Yes, we used to play every day after school.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وَمَاذَا كُنْتُمْ تَفْعَلُونَ فِي الصَّيْف؟
dialogue.transliteration: wa maadhaa kuntum taf3aloona fee as-sayf?
dialogue.english: And what did you used to do in the summer?

dialogue.speaker: Hala
dialogue.arabic: كُنَّا نَذْهَبُ إِلَى بَيْتِ جَدِّي فِي الْقَرْيَة.
dialogue.transliteration: kunnaa nadh-habu ilaa bayti jaddee fee al-qarya.
dialogue.english: We used to go to my grandfather's house in the village.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وَمَاذَا كَانَتْ تَفْعَلُ جَدَّتُكِ؟
dialogue.english: And what did your grandmother used to do?

dialogue.speaker: Hala
dialogue.arabic: كَانَتْ تَحْكِي لَنَا قِصَصًا قَبْلَ النَّوْم.
dialogue.transliteration: kaanat ta7kee lanaa qisasan qabla an-nawm.
dialogue.english: She used to tell us stories before sleeping.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: يَبْدُو أَنَّ الْحَيَاةَ كَانَتْ أَبْسَط.
dialogue.english: It seems life was simpler.

dialogue.speaker: Hala
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، كَانَتْ أَبْسَطَ بِكَثِير.
dialogue.english: Yes, it was much simpler.

response.arabic: نَشَأْتُ فِي حَيٍّ قَدِيمٍ فِي دِمَشْق.
response.english: I grew up in an old neighborhood in Damascus.

pair.transliteration: maadhaa kunta taf3alu wa anta sagheer?
pair.english: What did you used to do when you were young?

response.english: I used to play in the alley.

pair.english: Were you afraid of the dark?

response.english: Yes, I used to be very afraid.

lessons.culture: Fusha tells childhood memories with كَانَ plus a present-tense verb, which means 'used to', so كُنْتُ أَلْعَبُ is 'I used to play'. Grandparents and the village summer are a common shared memory in stories told across the Arab world.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you, a man: 'أَيْنَ نَشَأْتَ؟'. Say you grew up in Damascus.
exercises.tip: نَشَأْتُ means 'I grew up'.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: 'مَاذَا كُنْتَ تَفْعَلُ وَأَنْتَ صَغِير؟'. Say you used to play in the alley.
exercises.tip: كُنْتُ plus a present-tense verb means 'I used to'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: '_____ نَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ فِي الزُّقَاق.' (We used to play soccer in the alley.)
exercises.tip: كُنَّا is 'we were'; before a verb it means 'we used to'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'كُنْتُ _____ مِنَ الظَّلَامِ كَثِيرًا.' (I used to be very afraid of the dark.)
exercises.tip: أَخَافُ is 'I fear'; مِنْ names what you fear.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I had a friend named Kareem.'
exercises.tip: كَانَ لِي is 'I had'; the thing had comes after it.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'My grandmother used to tell us stories.'
exercises.tip: كَانَتْ is the feminine form, because the grandmother is a woman.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'We used to walk to school together every day.'
exercises.answer: كُنَّا نَمْشِي إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ مَعًا كُلَّ يَوْم
accepted: كُنَّا نَمْشِي إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ مَعًا كُلَّ يَوْم
كنا نمشي إلى المدرسة معا كل يوم
كُنَّا نَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ مَشْيًا كُلَّ يَوْم
kunnaa namshee ilaa al-madrasati ma3an kulla yawm

too_formal.item: كُنَّا نِمْشِي عَالْمَدْرَسَة سَوَا كُلّ يَوْم

exercises.tip: مَعًا is 'together'; كُلَّ يَوْم is 'every day'.

exercises.prompt: Which word, put before a present-tense verb, means 'used to'?
exercises.tip: كَانَ plus a present-tense verb tells a habit in the past.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'Back then life was much simpler'?
options: فِي ذَلِكَ الْوَقْتِ كَانَتِ الْحَيَاةُ أَبْسَطَ بِكَثِير
exercises.answer: فِي ذَلِكَ الْوَقْتِ كَانَتِ الْحَيَاةُ أَبْسَطَ بِكَثِير
accepted: فِي ذَلِكَ الْوَقْتِ كَانَتِ الْحَيَاةُ أَبْسَطَ بِكَثِير
في ذلك الوقت كانت الحياة أبسط بكثير
fee dhaalika al-waqti kaanati al-7ayaatu absata bikatheer
exercises.tip: أَبْسَطَ is 'simpler'; بِكَثِير adds 'by a lot'.

exercises.prompt: Put the pieces in order: 'فِي الزُّقَاق / كُنَّا / كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ / نَلْعَبُ'.
exercises.answer: كُنَّا نَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ فِي الزُّقَاق
accepted: كُنَّا نَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ فِي الزُّقَاق
كنا نلعب كرة القدم في الزقاق
كُنَّا نَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ فِي الزُّقَاقِ
kunnaa nal3abu kurata al-qadami fee az-zuqaaq
exercises.tip: كُنَّا first, then the verb, then the game, then the place.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'حَمْرَاء / أَوَّلُ / كَانَتْ / امْتَلَكْتُهَا / دَرَّاجَةٍ'.

too_formal.item: أَوَّل سِيكِل كَانَ عِنْدِي كَانَ أَحْمَر

exercises.tip: Fusha puts 'the first bike' first, then 'I had it', then 'was red'.

phrases.arabic: سَقَطْتُ عَلَى السُّلَّمِ وَأُصِبْتُ فِي رِجْلِي
phrases.transliteration: saqattu 3alaa as-sullami wa usibtu fee rijlee

phrases.arabic: أَخْطَأْتُ وَأَرْسَلْتُ الرِّسَالَةَ إِلَى الشَّخْصِ الْخَطَأ
phrases.transliteration: akhta2tu wa arsaltu ar-risaalata ilaa ash-shakhsi al-khata2
nimtu katheeran wa lam asma3i al-munabbih

dialogue.speaker: Dina
dialogue.arabic: مَا بِكَ يَا طَارِق؟ تَبْدُو مُتْعَبًا.
dialogue.transliteration: maa bika yaa Taariq? tabdoo mut3aban.
dialogue.english: What's wrong, Tariq? You look tired.

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.arabic: كَانَ صَبَاحِي سَيِّئًا. نِمْتُ كَثِيرًا وَلَمْ أَسْمَعِ الْمُنَبِّه.
dialogue.transliteration: kaana sabaa7ee sayyi2an. nimtu katheeran wa lam asma3i al-munabbih.
dialogue.english: My morning was bad. I overslept and didn't hear the alarm.

dialogue.speaker: Dina
dialogue.arabic: إِذًا تَأَخَّرْتَ عَنِ الْعَمَل؟
dialogue.english: So you were late for work?

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، تَأَخَّرْتُ عَنِ الْعَمَلِ هَذَا الصَّبَاح.
dialogue.english: Yes, I was late for work this morning.

dialogue.speaker: Dina
dialogue.arabic: وَمَاذَا حَدَثَ بَعْدَ ذَلِك؟
dialogue.english: And what happened after that?

dialogue.speaker: Dina
dialogue.arabic: هَذَا مُؤْسِف! وَكَيْفَ دَفَعْتَ؟
dialogue.english: That's a pity! And how did you pay?

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.arabic: اِسْتَعَرْتُ مَالًا مِنْ زَمِيلِي. وَأَمْسِ اِنْكَسَرَ هَاتِفِي أَيْضًا.
dialogue.transliteration: ista3artu maalan min zameelee. wa amsi inkasara haatifee aydan.
dialogue.english: I borrowed money from my colleague. And yesterday my phone broke too.

dialogue.speaker: Dina
dialogue.arabic: هَذَا كَثِير! هَلْ أَصْلَحْتَهُ؟
dialogue.english: That's a lot! Did you fix it?

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.arabic: ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الْمَحَلِّ، وَسَيَكُونُ جَاهِزًا غَدًا.
dialogue.transliteration: dhahabtu ilaa al-ma7alli, wa sayakoonu jaahizan ghadan.
dialogue.english: I went to the shop, and it will be ready tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Dina
dialogue.arabic: أَرْجُو أَنْ يَكُونَ غَدُكَ أَفْضَل.
dialogue.english: I hope your tomorrow is better.

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.arabic: شُكْرًا، إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه.
dialogue.english: Thank you, God willing.

response.transliteration: nimtu katheeran wa lam asma3i al-munabbih.
response.english: I overslept and didn't hear the alarm.

lessons.culture: When something goes wrong, Fusha speakers name what happened in a short past-tense sentence and often add الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه if it was not worse. Things that happen to you, such as a broken phone, are said about the object: اِنْكَسَرَ هَاتِفِي, 'my phone broke', not 'I broke'.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: 'لِمَاذَا تَأَخَّرْتَ؟'. Say you overslept and did not hear the alarm.
accepted: nimtu katheeran wa lam asma3i al-munabbih
exercises.tip: لَمْ plus a present-tense verb says 'did not'.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: 'مَا الَّذِي حَدَثَ؟'. Say your phone broke.
exercises.tip: The verb comes first and the thing that broke follows it.

exercises.prompt: Complete: '_____ مِفْتَاحَ الْبَيْت.' (I lost the house key.)
exercises.tip: أَضَعْتُ is 'I lost' something; ضَاعَ is 'got lost' by itself.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'نَسِيتُ _____ فِي الْبَيْت.' (I forgot my wallet at home.)
exercises.tip: The ending ـي on مِحْفَظَتِي means 'my'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'My bag got lost at the airport.'
exercises.tip: ضَاعَتْ ends in تْ because حَقِيبَة is feminine.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'I cut my hand while cooking.'
exercises.tip: أَثْنَاءَ means 'during'; وَأَنَا plus a verb means 'while I'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'The power went out all night.'
exercises.tip: طَوَالَ means 'throughout'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'The car broke down in the middle of the road'?
exercises.tip: مُنْتَصَفُ is 'the middle of'.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'I forgot'?
exercises.tip: أَضَعْتُ is 'I lost', جَرَحْتُ is 'I cut', سَقَطْتُ is 'I fell'.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'الْمَطَار / فِي / حَقِيبَتِي / ضَاعَتْ'.
exercises.tip: Verb first, then the bag, then the place.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'الْمُنَبِّه / أَسْمَعِ / وَلَمْ / نِمْتُ / كَثِيرًا'.
accepted: nimtu katheeran wa lam asma3i al-munabbih
exercises.tip: Two actions joined by وَ: what you did, then what did not happen.

phrases.arabic: قِيلَ لِي إِنَّكَ سَتَنْتَقِلُ إِلَى بَيْتٍ جَدِيد
phrases.transliteration: qeela lee innaka satantaqilu ilaa baytin jadeed

phrases.arabic: لَسْنَا مُتَأَكِّدِينَ بَعْدُ، رُبَّمَا هِيَ مُجَرَّدُ إِشَاعَة
phrases.transliteration: lasnaa muta2akkideena ba3d, rubbamaa hiya mujarradu ishaa3a

phrases.arabic: لَنْ تُصَدِّقَ مَا حَدَثَ أَمْسِ فِي الْحَيّ
phrases.transliteration: lan tusaddiqa maa 7adatha amsi fee al-7ayy

phrases.arabic: لَا تُخْبِرْ أَحَدًا، لَكِنِّي سَمِعْتُ أَنَّهُمْ سَيُسَافِرُونَ
phrases.transliteration: laa tukhbir a7adan, lakinnee sami3tu annahum sayusaafiroon

phrases.arabic: هَذَا كُلُّهُ كَلَامُ النَّاسِ، لَا أَعْرِفُ هَلْ هُوَ صَحِيحٌ أَمْ لَا
phrases.transliteration: haadhaa kulluhu kalaamu an-naas, laa a3rifu hal huwa sa7eeh am laa

dialogue.speaker: Maha
dialogue.arabic: مَرْحَبًا يَا يُوسُف. مَا آخِرُ أَخْبَارِكَ؟
dialogue.transliteration: marhaban yaa Yoosuf. maa aakhiru akhbaarika?
dialogue.english: Hello, Yousef. What's your latest news?

dialogue.speaker: Yousef
dialogue.arabic: أَهْلًا يَا مَهَا. عِنْدِي خَبَرٌ لَنْ تُصَدِّقِيهِ.
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan yaa Mahaa. 3indee khabarun lan tusaddiqeehi.
dialogue.english: Hello, Maha. I have news you won't believe.

dialogue.speaker: Maha
dialogue.arabic: مَاذَا حَدَثَ؟
dialogue.english: What happened?

dialogue.speaker: Maha
dialogue.arabic: حَقًّا؟ مَنْ أَخْبَرَكَ بِهَذَا الْخَبَر؟
dialogue.english: Really? Who told you this news?

dialogue.speaker: Yousef
dialogue.arabic: قَالَ لِي جَارُنَا. وَيَقُولُونَ إِنَّ مَحَلَّ فُلَانٍ أُغْلِقَ أَيْضًا.
dialogue.transliteration: qaala lee jaarunaa. wa yaqooloona inna ma7alla fulaanin ughliqa aydan.
dialogue.english: Our neighbor told me. And they say that such-and-such shop closed too.

dialogue.speaker: Yousef
dialogue.arabic: أَنْتِ عَلَى حَقٍّ، هَذَا كُلُّهُ كَلَامُ النَّاس.
dialogue.english: You're right, it's all just people's talk.

dialogue.speaker: Maha
dialogue.arabic: وَعِنْدِي أَنَا أَيْضًا خَبَرٌ: تَزَوَّجَتْ أُخْتِي الشَّهْرَ الْمَاضِي.
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3indee anaa aydan khabarun: tazawwajat ukhtee ash-shahra al-maadee.
dialogue.english: And I have news too: my sister got married last month.

dialogue.speaker: Yousef
dialogue.arabic: مَا شَاءَ اللَّه! وَسَمِعْنَا أَنَّ جِيرَانَنَا رُزِقُوا بِوَلَد.
dialogue.transliteration: maa shaa2a allaah! wa sami3naa anna jeeranaa ruziqoo biwalad.
dialogue.english: God has willed it! And we heard our neighbors had a baby boy.

dialogue.speaker: Maha
dialogue.arabic: مَا شَاءَ اللَّه! لَا تُخْبِرْ أَحَدًا، لَكِنِّي سَمِعْتُ أَنَّ جِيرَانَنَا سَيُسَافِرُونَ بَعْدَ شَهْر.
dialogue.transliteration: maa shaa2a allaah! laa tukhbir a7adan, lakinnee sami3tu anna jeeranaa sayusaafiroona ba3da shahr.
dialogue.english: God has willed it! Don't tell anyone, but I heard our neighbors are going to travel in a month.

dialogue.speaker: Yousef
dialogue.arabic: لَنْ أُخْبِرَ أَحَدًا. سَأَرَاكِ غَدًا.
dialogue.english: I won't tell anyone. I'll see you tomorrow.

response.english: I heard it from our neighbor.

pair.english: When did your sister get married?

lessons.culture: News travels by word of mouth, so Fusha has careful ways to say how sure you are: سَمِعْتُ أَنَّ is 'I heard that', يَقُولُونَ is 'they say', and رُبَّمَا is 'maybe'. On good news people answer مَا شَاءَ اللَّه, and on passing on a secret they add لَا تُخْبِرْ أَحَدًا.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: 'مَا آخِرُ أَخْبَارِكَ؟'. Say you have news they won't believe.
exercises.tip: لَنْ plus a present-tense verb says 'will never'.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: 'هَلْ هَذَا صَحِيح؟'. Say you are not sure yet.
exercises.tip: لَسْتُ is 'I am not'; a woman says مُتَأَكِّدَةً.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'سَمِعْتُ _____ سَامِرًا أَصْبَحَ مَخْطُوبًا.' (I heard that Samer got engaged.)
exercises.tip: After سَمِعْتُ, the word أَنَّ means 'that' and the name after it takes a fatha.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'مَنْ _____ بِهَذَا الْخَبَر؟' (Who told you this news? to a man)
exercises.tip: أَخْبَرَكَ is 'told you'; كَ is 'you' to a man, كِ to a woman.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'My sister got married last month.'
exercises.tip: الشَّهْرَ الْمَاضِي is 'last month', literally 'the past month'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Who told you this news?' (to a man)
exercises.tip: بِ joins the verb to what you were told about.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'They say the shop closed.'
exercises.tip: يَقُولُونَ is 'they say'; إِنَّ introduces what they say.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'That's all just people's talk'?
exercises.tip: كَلَامُ النَّاسِ is 'what people say', talk that may not be true.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'rumor'?
exercises.tip: خَبَر is 'news', حَقِيقَة is 'truth', مُفَاجَأَة is 'surprise'.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'الْخَبَر؟ / بِهَذَا / أَخْبَرَكَ / مَنْ'.
exercises.tip: مَنْ first, then the verb, then what you were told.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'الْمَاضِي / أُخْتِي / تَزَوَّجَتْ / الشَّهْرَ'.
exercises.tip: The verb comes first and agrees with أُخْت, so it is feminine.

phrases.arabic: سَافَرْتُ إِلَى مَدِينَةٍ أُخْرَى الْأُسْبُوعَ الْمَاضِي
phrases.transliteration: safartu ilaa madeenatin ukhraa al-usboo3a al-maadee

phrases.arabic: أَقَمْتُ فِي فُنْدُقٍ صَغِيرٍ قُرْبَ الْبَحْر
phrases.transliteration: aqamtu fee funduqin sagheerin qurba al-ba7r

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: أَيْنَ كُنْتِ يَا سَلْمَى؟ لَمْ أَرَكِ مُنْذُ أُسْبُوع.
dialogue.transliteration: ayna kunti yaa Salmaa? lam araki mundhu usboo3.
dialogue.english: Where were you, Salma? I have not seen you for a week.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: كَيْفَ سَافَرْتِ؟
dialogue.english: How did you travel?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: رَكِبْتُ الْقِطَارَ، وَاشْتَرَيْتُ التَّذْكِرَةَ قَبْلَ يَوْمٍ.
dialogue.transliteration: rakibtu al-qiTaara, washtaraytu at-tadhkirata qabla yawm.
dialogue.english: I took the train, and I bought the ticket the day before.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: كَمِ اسْتَغْرَقَتِ الرِّحْلَة؟
dialogue.english: How long did the journey take?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: اِسْتَغْرَقَتْ أَرْبَعَ سَاعَات. جَلَسْتُ بِجَانِبِ النَّافِذَة.
dialogue.transliteration: istaghraqat arba3a saa3aat. jalastu bijaanibi an-naafidha.
dialogue.english: It took four hours. I sat next to the window.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: وَمَاذَا رَأَيْتِ؟
dialogue.english: And what did you see?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: وَأَيْنَ أَقَمْتِ؟
dialogue.english: And where did you stay?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: أَقَمْتُ فِي فُنْدُقٍ صَغِيرٍ قُرْبَ الْبَحْرِ، وَالْتَقَطْتُ صُوَرًا كَثِيرَة.
dialogue.transliteration: aqamtu fee funduqin sagheerin qurba al-ba7ri, wa-ltaqaTtu suwaran katheera.
dialogue.english: I stayed in a small hotel near the sea, and I took many photos.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: هَلْ جَرَّبْتِ الْأَكْلَ الْمَحَلِّيّ؟
dialogue.english: Did you try the local food?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، وَعُدْتُ مُتْعَبَةً لَكِنْ سَعِيدَة.
dialogue.english: Yes, and I came back tired but happy.

response.english: It was wonderful, praise be to Allah.

pair.english: How long did the trip take?

lessons.culture: A person returning from a journey is welcomed with الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى السَّلَامَة, 'praise be to Allah for your safety'. Travelers ask Allah for a safe trip before leaving, and tell the story of the trip afterwards with الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه. Past events use the verb in its past form: سَافَرْتُ, رَكِبْتُ, وَصَلْنَا.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: 'كَمِ اسْتَغْرَقَتِ الرِّحْلَة؟'. Say four hours.
exercises.tip: اِسْتَغْرَقَتْ is 'it took' for a feminine thing like الرِّحْلَة.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: 'هَلْ جَرَّبْتَ الْأَكْلَ الْمَحَلِّيّ؟'. Say yes, you tried it.
exercises.tip: جَرَّبْتُ is 'I tried'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'اشْتَرَيْتُ _____ قَبْلَ يَوْمٍ' (I bought the ticket the day before.)
exercises.tip: اِشْتَرَيْتُ is 'I bought' and التَّذْكِرَةَ is the thing bought.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'أَقَمْتُ فِي فُنْدُقٍ صَغِيرٍ _____ الْبَحْر' (I stayed in a small hotel near the sea.)
exercises.tip: قُرْبَ means 'near'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I took the train from the main station.'
exercises.tip: رَكِبْتُ is 'I rode, I took (a vehicle)'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I packed my suitcase the night before.'
exercises.tip: جَهَّزْتُ is 'I prepared'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'We arrived after noon.'
exercises.tip: وَصَلْنَا is 'we arrived'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'The journey took four hours.'?
exercises.tip: اِسْتَغْرَقَ means 'it took (time)'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'I came back tired but happy.'?
options: سَافَرْتُ إِلَى مَدِينَةٍ أُخْرَى الْأُسْبُوعَ الْمَاضِي
exercises.tip: لَكِنْ means 'but'.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'بِجَانِبِ / النَّافِذَة / جَلَسْتُ'.
exercises.tip: The verb comes first, then where.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'الْمَاضِي / الْأُسْبُوعَ / أُخْرَى / مَدِينَةٍ / إِلَى / سَافَرْتُ'.
exercises.answer: سَافَرْتُ إِلَى مَدِينَةٍ أُخْرَى الْأُسْبُوعَ الْمَاضِي
accepted: سَافَرْتُ إِلَى مَدِينَةٍ أُخْرَى الْأُسْبُوعَ الْمَاضِي
سافرت إلى مدينة أخرى الأسبوع الماضي
safartu ilaa madeenatin ukhraa al-usboo3a al-maadee
exercises.tip: The verb comes first, then where to, then when.

phrases.arabic: سَيَكُونُ عِنْدَنَا مَوْلُودٌ جَدِيدٌ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه
phrases.transliteration: sayakoonu 3indanaa mawloodun jadeedun in shaa2a allaah

phrases.arabic: عَادَ أَبِي مِنَ الْمُسْتَشْفَى وَهُوَ بِخَيْرٍ الْآن
phrases.transliteration: 3aada abee mina al-mustashfaa wahuwa bikhayrin al-aan

phrases.arabic: مَبْرُوك، أَنَا سَعِيدٌ جِدًّا مِنْ أَجْلِكَ
phrases.transliteration: mabrook, ana sa3eedun jiddan min ajlika

reply.english: May Allah reward you with good.

dialogue.speaker: Yasir
dialogue.arabic: عِنْدِي لَكَ خَبَرٌ سَارّ يَا بِلَال.
dialogue.english: I have good news for you, Bilal.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: خَيْرًا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه، مَاذَا حَدَثَ؟
dialogue.english: Good, Allah willing, what happened?

dialogue.speaker: Yasir
dialogue.arabic: بَارَكَ اللَّهُ فِيكَ. وَاشْتَرَيْنَا أَيْضًا بَيْتًا جَدِيدًا.
dialogue.transliteration: baaraka allaahu feeka. washtarayna aydan baytan jadeedan.
dialogue.english: May Allah bless you. And we also bought a new house.

dialogue.speaker: Yasir
dialogue.arabic: وَتَمَّتْ خِطْبَةُ أَخِي أَمْسِ.
dialogue.english: And my brother got engaged yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ فِيهِ، أَخْبَارٌ جَمِيلَةٌ كَثِيرَة!
dialogue.transliteration: baaraka allaahu lakum feehi, akhbaarun jameelatun katheera!
dialogue.english: May Allah bless it for you, so much beautiful news!

dialogue.speaker: Yasir
dialogue.arabic: وَعَادَ أَبِي مِنَ الْمُسْتَشْفَى وَهُوَ بِخَيْرٍ الْآن.
dialogue.transliteration: wa3aada abee mina al-mustashfaa wahuwa bikhayrin al-aan.
dialogue.english: And my father came back from the hospital and he is well now.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: اِلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى سَلَامَتِهِ. لِنَحْتَفِلْ مَعًا هَذَا الْمَسَاء.
dialogue.transliteration: al-7amdu lillaahi 3alaa salaamatihi. lina7tafil ma3an haadhaa al-masaa2.
dialogue.english: Praise be to Allah for his safety. Let us celebrate together this evening.

dialogue.speaker: Yasir
dialogue.arabic: فِكْرَةٌ جَمِيلَة! سَأُخْبِرُ الْجَمِيع.
dialogue.english: A beautiful idea! I will tell everyone.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: مَبْرُوك مَرَّةً أُخْرَى يَا صَدِيقِي.
dialogue.english: Congratulations once more, my friend.

pair.english: I have good news for you.

response.arabic: خَيْرًا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه، مَا هُوَ؟
response.transliteration: khayran in shaa2a allaah, maa huwa?
response.english: Good, Allah willing, what is it?
Congratulations, I am happy for you.

pair.english: When did you hear the news?
May Allah bless it for you.

response.english: May Allah reward you with good.

lessons.culture: Sharing good news and rejoicing for others is encouraged in Islam, and the first answer is مَبْرُوك or بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لَكَ فِيه. The person who has the news credits Allah with الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه, and says إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه for good things still to come. Friends then plan to celebrate together.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: 'عِنْدِي لَكَ خَبَرٌ سَارّ'. Ask what it is, Allah willing.
exercises.answer: خَيْرًا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه، مَاذَا حَدَثَ؟
accepted: خَيْرًا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه، مَاذَا حَدَثَ؟
خيرا إن شاء الله، ماذا حدث؟
exercises.tip: خَيْرًا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه is 'good, Allah willing'.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: 'حَصَلْتُ عَلَى الْوَظِيفَة'. Congratulate him.
exercises.answer: مَبْرُوك، أَنَا سَعِيدٌ جِدًّا مِنْ أَجْلِكَ
accepted: مَبْرُوك، أَنَا سَعِيدٌ جِدًّا مِنْ أَجْلِكَ
مبروك، أنا سعيد جدا من أجلك
mabrook, ana sa3eedun jiddan min ajlika
exercises.tip: مِنْ أَجْلِكَ is 'for your sake'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'نَجَحْتُ فِي _____' (I passed the exam!)
exercises.tip: الِامْتِحَان means 'the exam'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'مَبْرُوك، أَنَا _____ جِدًّا مِنْ أَجْلِكَ' (Congratulations, I am very happy for you. (to a man))
exercises.tip: سَعِيدٌ means 'happy'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'We bought a new house.'
exercises.tip: اِشْتَرَيْنَا is 'we bought'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'When did you hear the news?'
exercises.tip: مَتَى is 'when'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Let us celebrate together this evening.'
exercises.tip: لِنَحْتَفِلْ is 'let us celebrate'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'We will have a new baby, Allah willing.'?
options: سَيَكُونُ عِنْدَنَا مَوْلُودٌ جَدِيدٌ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه
عَادَ أَبِي مِنَ الْمُسْتَشْفَى وَهُوَ بِخَيْرٍ الْآن
exercises.answer: سَيَكُونُ عِنْدَنَا مَوْلُودٌ جَدِيدٌ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه
accepted: سَيَكُونُ عِنْدَنَا مَوْلُودٌ جَدِيدٌ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه
سيكون عندنا مولود جديد إن شاء الله
sayakoonu 3indanaa mawloodun jadeedun in shaa2a allaah
exercises.tip: مَوْلُود means 'a newborn'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'Praise be to Allah, this is a great blessing.'?
options: مَبْرُوك، أَنَا سَعِيدٌ جِدًّا مِنْ أَجْلِكَ
exercises.tip: نِعْمَة means 'a blessing'.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'أَمْسِ / أَخِي / خِطْبَةُ / تَمَّتْ'.
exercises.tip: The verb comes first, then who, then when.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'فِيه / لَكَ / اللَّهُ / بَارَكَ'.
exercises.tip: The blessing comes first, then who it is for.

challenge.title: Tell what happened
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation in Fusha between two friends. One asks what happened yesterday and the other tells a bad day: something broke or was lost, and how the night went. Then one friend shares a piece of news, the other asks who said it, and they agree it may only be a rumor. Add one memory from childhood told with كَانَ plus a present-tense verb.
required_elements: a question about yesterday and an answer in the past tense
something that went wrong, such as a lost or broken thing
a piece of news with سَمِعْتُ أَنَّ
a question about who said it and a doubt that it is true
a childhood memory with كُنَّا or كُنْتُ plus a verb
a plan to meet with سَأَرَاكَ or سَأَرَاكِ

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: مَرْحَبًا يَا دِينَا. مَاذَا فَعَلْتِ أَمْسِ؟
dialogue.transliteration: marhaban yaa Deenaa. maadhaa fa3alti amsi?
dialogue.english: Hello, Dina. What did you do yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Dina
dialogue.arabic: أَهْلًا يَا رَامِي. كَانَ أَمْسِ يَوْمًا سَيِّئًا. اِنْكَسَرَ هَاتِفِي وَأَضَعْتُ مِفْتَاحَ الْبَيْت.
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan yaa Raamee. kaana amsi yawman sayyi2an. inkasara haatifee wa adha3tu miftaa7a al-bayt.
dialogue.english: Hello, Rami. Yesterday was a bad day. My phone broke and I lost the house key.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: هَذَا مُؤْسِف! وَأَيْنَ كُنْتِ لَيْلَةَ أَمْسِ؟
dialogue.transliteration: haadhaa mu2sif! wa ayna kunti laylata amsi?
dialogue.english: That's a pity! And where were you last night?

dialogue.speaker: Dina
dialogue.arabic: كُنْتُ فِي الْبَيْتِ، وَانْقَطَعَتِ الْكَهْرَبَاءُ طَوَالَ اللَّيْل.
dialogue.transliteration: kuntu fee al-bayti, wa inqata3ati al-kahrabaa2u tawaala al-layl.
dialogue.english: I was at home, and the power went out all night.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: وَعِنْدِي أَنَا خَبَرٌ: سَمِعْتُ أَنَّ سَامِرًا أَصْبَحَ مَخْطُوبًا.
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3indee anaa khabarun: sami3tu anna Saameran asba7a makhtooban.
dialogue.english: And I have news: I heard that Samer got engaged.

dialogue.speaker: Dina
dialogue.arabic: حَقًّا؟ مَنْ أَخْبَرَكَ بِهَذَا الْخَبَر؟
dialogue.english: Really? Who told you this news?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: جَارُنَا. لَكِنَّنَا لَسْنَا مُتَأَكِّدِينَ بَعْدُ.
dialogue.english: Our neighbor. But we're not sure yet.

dialogue.speaker: Dina
dialogue.arabic: عِنْدَمَا كُنَّا صِغَارًا، كُنَّا نَلْعَبُ مَعَ سَامِرٍ فِي الزُّقَاق.
dialogue.transliteration: 3indamaa kunnaa sighaaran, kunnaa nal3abu ma3a Saamirin fee az-zuqaaq.
dialogue.english: When we were young, we used to play with Samer in the alley.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: صَحِيح، كَانَتِ الْحَيَاةُ أَبْسَطَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْوَقْت.
dialogue.transliteration: sa7eeh, kaanati al-7ayaatu absata fee dhaalika al-waqt.
dialogue.english: True, life was simpler back then.

dialogue.speaker: Dina
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ. سَأَرَاكَ غَدًا.
dialogue.english: Yes. I'll see you tomorrow.
